title: Young Muslims
hookLine: youth groups, nasheed, online study circles

lines: A PAGE OF TAFSIR, LINE BY LINE.
cards: A Thursday night video call. Small squares on a screen: a student in a dorm room with headphones on, a young nurse just off shift, someone in a parked car with the dome light on.
One shares a page of tafsir, a commentary on the Qur'an, and they read it together, line by line, and argue gently about what it means. Somebody's little brother wanders into frame and waves.
Nobody planned this in a mosque office. They planned it in a group chat.

teach.h: THE CAVE: YOUNG MEN WHO BELIEVED.
teach.b: The Qur'an has its own pictures of the young, starting in a cave.
Surah al-Kahf tells of the people of the cave, in Pickthall's words: "Lo! they were young men who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance."
Young people, holding on in a city that didn't share their faith. Elsewhere, Ibrahim's people describe him as a youth, the young man who spoke against their idols.

teach.h: SHADE FOR ONE WHO GREW UP FAITHFUL.
teach.b: In al-Bukhari, among those the Prophet, peace be upon him, says Allah will shade on a day when there is no other shade, he names, in paraphrase, a young person who grew up in the worship of Allah.
Growing up faithful is named on its own, in the same list as the just ruler. And now?
Mosque youth groups and campus student associations run study circles, sports nights, food drives and late Ramadan iftars.

Nasheed, songs of praise and devotion, are sung by young voices, some with only voice and drum, because some scholars discourage instruments, and some with instruments, because others permit them; day one hundred forty-eight looked at why scholars differ.
Online study circles gather young people from different cities around a text.
And the hard part, said plainly: some young Muslims carry questions about identity, about belonging, about the distance between their parents' customs and their own lives.
They also carry the faith forward into new languages and new places. The people of the cave didn't wait to be old enough to matter, and neither does the Thursday night call.

how: Young Muslims gather in mosque youth groups and campus student associations for study circles, service projects and iftars, sing and share nasheed, and join online study circles that read the Qur'an and its commentaries together.

o: a youth wing run by a mosque's main office
the young who carry the faith into new places
Muslims too young to be asked to pray yet

p: a youth faithful from the start
shaded on a day without shade

s: the Qur'an calls the people of the cave young men
"Lo! they were young men who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance."
scholars all agree about instruments in nasheed
some discourage instruments, others permit them, so some nasheed use only voice and drum.
the hadith of the shade leaves out the young
it names a young person who grew up in the worship of Allah.

games.q: you're one of the young men of the cave, in a city that doesn't share your faith. what do you do?
o: go along quietly with the city.
withdraw together to a cave and ask your Lord for mercy.
wait until you're older to decide.
games.why: in al-Kahf they take refuge in the cave together and ask their Lord for mercy, and Allah increases them in guidance.

practice: Think of someone younger whose life you touch, a child, a niece, a student, a teenager down the street, and one thing they're trying to do: learn, build, believe, belong.
For a few breaths, simply wish them well in it, and if you pray, ask Allah to increase them in guidance, in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Young Muslims. From the young men of the cave to youth groups, nasheed and online study circles, the young who carry the faith into new places. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: young men, youths; the Qur'an's word for the people of the cave.

carryVoice: Your line: the young carry it. Into new languages and new places. See you tomorrow.
